Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal on our side flagged two items in the draft partner paper that could block procurement: (1) the pass-through tax and fee allocation — they want explicit language that marketplace commissions and third-party pass-through fees are borne by StratusExchange unless otherwise detailed in an order form; and (2) a clear waterfall for invoicing and dispute routing so tax withholding doesn't cascade to platform liability.

Can you share your legal/ops view on a simple waterfall that keeps revenue recognition clean for both sides? We can accept a limited carveout for platform indemnity if there's a reciprocal audit right. Attaching the draft addendum we used as a starting point.

Ideal timeline from our side: confirm language by EOW so we can get procurement sign-off next week.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Marketplace addendum — pass-through/tax allocation

Samantha — thanks for the clear flags. I've sketched a pragmatic approach that legal and billing can live with:

- Short summary of proposal (see attached):
  1) Marketplace fees and third-party pass-through taxes/fees are the reseller's responsibility unless explicitly itemized on the Order Form.
  2) Billing waterfall: StratusExchange invoices end customer -> Redwood invoices StratusExchange for platform fees net of marketplace commissions; tax withholding responsibility is on the invoicing party as listed on the Order Form.
  3) Dispute routing: disputes about marketplace commission rates or third-party fees are routed to reseller (StratusExchange) and do not delay Redwood's invoicing for platform usage; disputed amounts can be escrowed pending resolution.
  4) Limited indemnity: Redwood will cover platform liabilities from breaches of our service; reseller responsible for marketplace integrations and third-party compliance. Audit rights are reciprocal but scoped to billing records for a 12-month lookback with notice.

I've attached: Stratus_Marketplace_Addendum_Redline_v1.docx and a short PassThrough_Waterfall.pdf that maps the invoice flow. Ben/Laura — can you confirm whether the 12-month audit window and escrow approach are acceptable from ops/legal?

Marissa Cole
Head of Partner Sales | Redwood Inference

Marissa / team — reviewed the redline and Ben's operational suggestion. High-level comments attached (legal_redline_comments.docx). Summary:

- Pass-through allocation: we can accept a clause stating reseller is responsible for marketplace commissions and third-party taxes so long as the Order Form explicitly lists any tax withholding obligations for the invoicing party. Add an "Order Form controls" sentence.
- 60-day suspension remedy: acceptable if we provide an express carve-out that suspension does not relieve Redwood of SLA credit obligations already accrued and must be preceded by 30 days' written notice and cure period tied to invoicing-specific delinquencies.
- Indemnity and audit: reciprocal audit for billing records is OK but limit to a single audit per 12 months unless material discrepancies are identified. Keep escrow as an operational option but cap escrow to disputed amount.

I'll incorporate these edits into the redline and re-upload. Ops, please confirm the notice/cure mechanics so we can finalize language.
